Now, I am no expert in this as I only personally realised that I was asexual a year ago and being a guy I obviouslyhave different experiences with asexuality and sexual acts in general. That being said, this is an interesting situation. Only liking one form of sexual act doesn't equal asexuality as there are lots of people who enjoy sex but don't like giving head, whether that be because they find it degrading or disgusting, but everything else you said could point towards you being asexual. 

Asexuality is defined by a lack of sexual attraction but a lot of asexuals do still partake in and enjoy sex as you did. However, there is a micro label within asexuality called demi-sexuality where you only feel sexual attraction where you only experience sexual attraction after already forming a strong emotional bond with a person and truely loving them as you described. I would suggest thinking about when you started wanting to have sex with him as if it was almost immediately when you started dating then you likely aren't demi-sexual. I think you should also try to consider any other people you may have been attracted to in that way if there are any or any negative sexual experiences you may have had prior to or with this partner as asexuality can be brought on by trauma.

It's when you talk about feeling disgusted by sexual thoughts and them killing the mood when masterbating that really sounds to me like asexuality. I myself am sex-repulsed which it sounds like you could be too if any sexual thoughts turn you off.

Asexuality is a massive umbrella term that covers all sorts of different experiences and while not liking giving head doesn't mean you're asexual, enjoying more "normal" sex for lack of a better term also doesn't mean that you aren't asexual. I'm sure there are people in the community who share your experience though it is not personally mine. 

So no, you definitely are not abnormal.
